Stores a batch of readings from an edge agent (at most 10,000), skipping ones already stored.

get.description: The templates an app can be made from, with their settings (what the form asks).

schema.title: Response List Templates App Templates Get

get.description:
How the browser signs in here: the OpenID Connect issuer and client, and whether requests
without a token act as the development user (anywhere but production). With `?org=<slug>`,
that organisation's own identity provider (T5.05): 404 if it has none.
Liveness: the process is up. Does not touch dependencies.

Who the request is from: email, name, organisation, and whether it signed in through the
identity provider (`oidc`) or is the development user (`dev`).

Your organisation, and whether you are its admin (an organisation admin, or someone whose
sign-in grants admin). The development identity names one with `?org=`, or gets the only one.

delete.description:
Removes your organisation's identity provider: its tokens stop working at once (each request
checks), and people sign in through this deployment's issuer again.

get.description: Your organisation's identity provider, or null when it signs in through this deployment's.

schema.title: Response Get Provider Org Identity Provider Get

put.description:
Sets your organisation's identity provider. A new issuer is pending until you sign in
through it as yourself (the same email): that shows your organisation controls it, so no
organisation can take another's. Then its tokens sign in to your organisation only. Turning
`enforced` on needs it confirmed and you signed in through it (409 otherwise), so a provider
that doesn't work can't lock everyone out; then no other sign-in reaches your organisation.

get.description:
Your organisation's own models, over HTTP and from GitHub, archived ones too, by key then
version (never their tokens or code).

schema.title: Response List Own Models Org Models Get

post.description:
Register a model version computed by your endpoint: its spec (inputs, outputs, bounded
parameters) and the https address Tiles posts each evaluation to. The host must be one the
deployment allows (`TILES_MODEL_HOSTS`). A design model takes no inputs; a virtual sensor at
least one. 409 if the version exists already: a version never changes, so give a new one.

Register a model version from a GitHub repository at a full commit SHA: the directory
(`path`) holds `tiles-model.json` (the spec, and the `entry` file, `model.py` unless named) and
the Python files, whose `run(inputs, params)` the sandbox calls (the standard library only).
The code is fetched once and kept, with its SHA-256; a private repository's token is used for
that and not kept. Needs the deployment's sandbox (`TILES_SANDBOX_URL`).

patch.description:
Archive a model version (or bring it back); for one over HTTP, also move its endpoint or set
or clear its token. Its spec, and a GitHub model's code, never change.

get.description: Your organisation's SCIM tokens, newest first (never the tokens themselves).

schema.title: Response List Scim Tokens Org Scim Tokens Get

post.description:
A token for your identity provider's SCIM client (`/scim/v2`), which then creates, updates
and deactivates your organisation's users. It is shown once; only its hash is kept.

delete.description: Revokes a SCIM token: it stops working at once.

get.description: Whether your organisation's sites record UX events (organisation admins).

put.description:
Turn UX analytics on or off for your organisation's sites (organisation admins). Off, nothing
is recorded; the events already kept stay until they are 90 days old.

get.description: Readiness: the database and Redis are reachable. 503 if either is not.
The resources: users only.
What this SCIM service supports (public, as RFC 7644 allows).

The organisation's users, with `filter=userName eq "…"` (or `externalId`, `emails.value`),
`startIndex` (from 1) and `count` (up to 200).

post.description:
Creates a user (they sign in later, and are linked by email). A user deleted before comes
back with their history; 409 if the email or externalId is an existing user's.

delete.description:
Deletes a user: they can't sign in, their site memberships end, and SCIM no longer finds
them. What they did stays in the history, under their name.

get.description: One user.

patch.description:
Changes a user with `Operations` (`add`, `replace`; `remove` of `externalId`), by path or
by a value object without one, as Entra ID sends them.

put.description: Replaces a user's attributes (those Tiles keeps).

get.description: Sites in your organisation (every site for the dev identity).

post.description:
Creates a site in your organisation, with you as its admin. Its slug must be new in the
organisation (409 otherwise).

get.description: The site's edge agents (not revoked ones) and whether each is online.

schema.title: Response List Agents Sites  Site Id  Agents Get

post.description: Register an agent (admins only). The answer holds its token, which is never shown again.

delete.description: Revoke an agent (admins only): its token stops working at once.

get.description: The site's apps, by number.

schema.title: Response List Apps Sites  Site Id  Apps Get

post.description:
Makes an app from a template's current version: 422 with what to fix if the settings don't
fit it.

delete.description: Archives an app: it leaves the list, and its number isn't reused.

put.description: Renames an app or changes its settings, for the template version it was made with.

post.description: Brings an archived app back to the list (the Undo after archiving one).

get.description: Runs the app on its signal's readings now: its status, in words, and the chart.
Every change on this site, newest first (admins only).

schema.title: Response Audit Log Sites  Site Id  Audit Get

post.description:
Replay a signal's history with each combination of detection settings and score the warnings
against the events given: recall, precision, false warnings per day and warning time, best first.

get.description:
Whether the copilot is set up on this API (an Anthropic API key and a model are configured),
and whether this site's admins have turned it on.
Your conversations on this site, the latest first.

schema.title: Response List Conversations Sites  Site Id  Copilot Conversations Get

post.description: Start a conversation with the copilot on this site; it is yours alone.

delete.description: Delete one of your conversations, unless the copilot is still answering in it (409).

get.description: One of your conversations, with its messages and the tools the copilot used.

post.description: Ask a question in the conversation; the answer streams back as server-sent events.

delete.description: Withdraw your rating of an answer.

put.description:
Rate one of your answers up or down, with a comment; your site's admins read it, with the
question and the answer, to improve the copilot.

get.description: The site's rated answers, newest first, with their question (admins).

schema.title: Response List Feedback Sites  Site Id  Copilot Feedback Get

put.description:
Turn the copilot on or off for this site (admins). On, each question and the tool results the
copilot reads to answer it (the site's data, as the user who asked may see it) go to the AI
provider.

get.description: The site's copilot usage by UTC day and by user, with the limits and today's budget (admins).
The site's datasets (batch tables), by name, with their columns and row counts.

schema.title: Response List Datasets Sites  Site Id  Datasets Get

post.description: Start a dataset with its columns; send its rows next.

delete.description: Delete a dataset and its rows (engineers and admins).

get.description: A dataset with its columns and its first 20 rows.

post.description:
Which variables separate the failed batches from the good ones: Cohen's d with its 95%
confidence interval and r, per segment of `split` if given, largest effect first.
Append a batch of rows (at most 5,000), in order.

get.description: The site's design projects, the one with the latest run first (T4.14).

schema.title: Response List Projects Sites  Site Id  Design Projects Get

post.description: Start a design project on this site; its name must be new on the site.

get.description: The site's detectors, by name, with their settings and state.

schema.title: Response List Detectors Sites  Site Id  Detectors Get

post.description:
Watch a signal: warn when it leaves its rolling baseline by `k` robust spreads for `persist`
readings in a row. It starts with the signal's stored history.

delete.description: Stop the detector. Its warnings stay; one still open ends now, since nothing will update it.

patch.description:
Set (or clear, with null) the asset the detector watches, to match its warnings to that
asset's events (T3.10).

post.description: Run the detector on one batch of its new readings now (`caught_up`: nothing more waiting).

get.description: The site's documents, newest first.

schema.title: Response List Documents Sites  Site Id  Documents Get

post.description:
Uploads a document: the body is the file (Content-Type `application/pdf`, `text/plain` or
`text/markdown`, up to 20 MB). Its text is read page by page and indexed for search; 422 says
why a file can't be read (encrypted, a scan without text, not UTF-8…).

parameters.description: One of english, german, french, spanish, italian, dutch, portuguese, swedish, simple
parameters.name: language

schema.description: One of english, german, french, spanish, italian, dutch, portuguese, swedish, simple
schema.title: Language

get.description:
The passages that match best, each with its document and page to cite. The query is read as
a web search: words (stemmed: "valves" finds "valve"), "quoted phrases", OR, and -words to
leave out.

delete.description: Archives a document: it leaves the list and search; its number isn't reused.

get.description: The file as it was uploaded (a PDF opens at a page with `#page=N`).

post.description: Brings an archived document back to the list and search (the Undo after archiving one).

get.description: The site's imports, newest first (the last 100).

schema.title: Response List Imports Sites  Site Id  Imports Get

post.description: Starts an import (engineers and admins). Its readings follow in batches.
Marks the import done; its counts are final.

One batch of an import's readings (at most 10,000). All or nothing: one invalid reading
and the batch is refused (422), naming it.

get.description: The site's insights, newest first; only those in one status if given.

post.description:
Save a finding: its evidence is computed from `source` now and kept as it is. It waits for
another engineer to accept or reject it.

delete.description: Delete an insight (its author, or an admin).

get.description:
A saved insight by its number: the finding, its query, the evidence kept with it, the proposed
actions and its review.

patch.description:
Change the title, summary or actions while it waits for review (its author, or an admin).
The query and evidence stay: a different finding is a new insight.

post.description: Back to waiting for review (its author, or an admin), e.g. to revise a rejected one.
Accept or reject it: another engineer than its author; rejecting says why.

get.description: Your membership of this site (joining it on first visit), including your role.

The site's members (everyone who has signed in to it) and their roles. Organisation admins are
admins of every site, listed here or not.

schema.title: Response List Members Sites  Site Id  Members Get

put.description: Change a member's role on this site (admins only; not your own).

get.description: The site's model bindings, with how their last run went.

schema.title: Response List Bindings Sites  Site Id  Model Bindings Get

post.description:
Bind a model version to the site's signals. Its outputs become new signals, <name>.<output>,
from source model:<key>@<version>; the runner fills them from then on, starting with the
history already stored.

delete.description: Stop running the binding. What it computed stays; its derived signals keep their readings.

post.description:
Run the binding on its new data now (one batch of readings: `caught_up` says whether more
is left, for the next call or the scheduled runs).

get.description:
Every model version the site can use, by key then version: the built-in ones, then its
organisation's own served over HTTP.

schema.title: Response List Models Sites  Site Id  Models Get

get.description: A model's versions, newest first.

schema.title: Response Model Versions Sites  Site Id  Models  Key  Get

post.description:
Run a model on the input series given (all one length) and its parameters (defaults if left out).

Nothing is stored: this is for trying a model; the runner (T3.03) writes derived signals. A
model served over HTTP whose endpoint fails gives 502.

get.description:
What was sent, what waits (to be retried, with why, if it failed), and what was given up,
newest first (admins).

schema.title: Response Deliveries Sites  Site Id  Notifications Get

get.description:
Which warnings reach you by email. Until you choose: those assigned to you, not every new one.
Like any change to a site, choosing needs engineer or above, and so does receiving them.

put.description:
Choose which warnings you are told about on this site: those raised, those assigned to you, or
both.

get.description: The site's Teams channel, which hears of every new warning (admins).

put.description:
Point the site at a Teams channel's webhook (Workflows, or an incoming webhook), or remove it.
The URL is a credential: it is stored sealed (T5.06) and never shown again.

get.description:
How far the site is set up, step by step: created, its plant outlined in the ontology, an
edge agent that has called in, tags mapped to Signal nodes, and a machine with mapped signals
(the first dashboard to open).
Commit history, newest first.

schema.title: Response Get History Sites  Site Id  Ontology Commits Get

post.description: Commit your staged changes.
Undo a commit by committing its inverse operations.

get.description: The committed ontology as a file: JSON (nodes, edges and where it came from) or CSV (one table).
The committed graph (`head`), or head plus your staged changes (`working`).

Health check: dangling or duplicate relationships, orphans and missing required properties.

Scores the committed graph by default; `view=working` includes your staged changes.

post.description:
Plan the changes that bring the committed ontology to the file's, and stage them (unless `dry_run`).

`merge` adds and sets; `replace` also removes what the file doesn't have. You then commit
them, or send them for review, like any staged change. Needs no staged changes of your own.
Pass the preview's `commit` as `expect_commit` to stage only what the preview showed.

get.description: Whether every ontology change on this site needs a review.

put.description: Require (or stop requiring) a review for every ontology change on this site (admins).

get.description: Change requests, newest first: open ones (default), closed ones (approved, rejected, withdrawn) or all.

schema.title: Response List Reviews Sites  Site Id  Ontology Reviews Get

post.description: Send your staged changes (or the revert of a commit) for review. Your staged changes move into the request.

get.description: A change request with its ops, its comments and, while open, whether it still applies.

post.description:
Approve a change request: its ops are committed, with its author as author and you as reviewer.
Not its author; its named reviewer if it has one, any engineer otherwise, or an admin.
Comment on a change request.

Reject a change request, saying why. Nothing is committed; its author can rework it.
Not its author; its named reviewer if it has one, any engineer otherwise, or an admin.

Take your change request back into your staged changes, to change and send again.

An open request is withdrawn; a rejected or withdrawn one stays as it is. A revert
is not staged (sent again it would no longer be a revert): an open one is only
withdrawn, and a closed one is requested again from the history.

delete.description: Throw away your staged changes. Open to every member, so a user demoted to viewer can drop old work.

get.description: Your staged changes to the ontology, not yet committed (each person stages their own).

schema.title: Response Get Staged Sites  Site Id  Ontology Staged Get

post.description: Stage one change. It is checked against your working graph; returns all your staged ops.

schema.title: Response Stage Op Sites  Site Id  Ontology Staged Post

post.description: Stage several changes, all or none (e.g. a node and its relationship). Returns all your staged ops.

schema.title: Response Stage Ops Sites  Site Id  Ontology Staged Batch Post

get.description:
The last `days`: each detector's warnings scored against its asset's events (an event caught
when a warning started within `horizon_hours` before it), with what people resolved them as.
`codes` (repeatable) counts only those events, e.g. the downtime codes the detectors target.

The site's runs, the latest first; of one model (a registry key or the browser's id) and one
project if named.

post.description:
Run a registered design model with these parameters and keep the result, computed here, as the
site's next numbered run, in a project and after a parent run if given.

get.description: What changed from run `a` to run `b` (of one model, in any versions).
A run by its number, with its inputs, results and lineage (the runs it was changed from).
Run `number`'s audit record, as JSON to keep (T4.13).
Run `number`'s audit record as a PDF report (T4.13).

post.description: Run `number`'s version and parameters again, as a new run after its model's latest run in its project.

Checks the quality of the site's signals (all, or those listed) over the `hours` up to each one's
latest reading, and stores each report as the signal's latest (engineers and admins). Audited.
A site of more than MAX_CHECK signals is checked whole with `tiles-check-quality`, not in a request.

get.description:
For each tag no ontology node is linked to: the node to link, or the Signal node to create (with the
ops to stage), with a score and the reasons.
One of the site's signals, with its settings, latest reading and data quality.

patch.description:
Sets a signal's unit, sample rate, description or ontology link (engineers and admins).
A link must name a Signal node of the committed ontology that no other tag is linked to.

get.description:
A signal's readings from `from` (included) to `to` (excluded): as they are when there are at
most `points`, otherwise in at most `points` buckets with their average, minimum and maximum.

post.description:
Has the signal's level moved from its baseline (a wearing tool's), how fast, and when does
it reach `limit`? The baseline is `baseline_hours` before the last `recent_hours` up to `end`.

get.description: The site's latest sweeps, without their results.

schema.title: Response List Sweeps Sites  Site Id  Sweeps Get

post.description: Start a sweep (202: it runs in the background), or answer from an identical one's result (200).

get.description: A sweep's progress (`done` of `total` points), and its result once done.

post.description: Stop a sweep: one still queued at once, a running one after the chunk it is on.

get.description:
Whether this site records UX events (its organisation turned them on): the browser sends
none otherwise.

post.description:
Records a batch of UX events from one browser session (any member). Nothing is stored unless
the organisation turned the analytics on, nor beyond an hour's share for the site and the
session. A retention policy lets events go 90 days on. Not audited: like a person's own
copilot conversations, they change nothing on the site, and are about using the app.

get.description:
How often each page, task, palette use, help topic and error came up on this site over the
last `days` days, and in how many browser sessions (admins). Counts only.

The site's warnings, newest first. `state`: the signal still out (open) or back (ended).
`status`: raised (nobody has looked yet), acknowledged, resolved, or unresolved (either of
the first two). `assignee`: me, none (unassigned), or a user's id.

parameters.description: me, none, or a user's id
parameters.name: assignee

schema.description: me, none, or a user's id
schema.title: Assignee
Response List Warnings Sites  Site Id  Warnings Get

get.description: One warning, with its detector's settings and its activity.

post.description: Say someone is looking at it.

put.description:
Assign it to an engineer or admin of the site (acknowledging it, if nobody had), or unassign
it (`user_id` null). Assigning it to whom it is already assigned only keeps the note, as a comment.

post.description: Add a note to its activity, whatever its status (without waiting on its other steps).
Undo a resolution (it stays acknowledged, and assigned).

Close it with its outcome: a true alarm, a false alarm, or unknown (acknowledging it, if
nobody had). Its signal may still be out.
